claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and undergoes rapid oxidation and degradation at high temperature.
Surface aluminization, such as pack cementation, can deposit a thin Al-enriched surface layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al-enriched surface layer will oxidize to form a continuous alumina scale.
Aluminization will produce a uniform and adherent Al2O3 scale on HfNbTaTiZr.
Surface Al will oxidize preferentially relative to the substrate constituents.
The resulting alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The alumina diffusion barrier will prevent rapid internal oxidation and degradation of HfNbTaTiZr.
Surface aluminization will not alter the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's useful mechanical properties.
At about 1000 °C in air for 50–100 hours, aluminized specimens will have lower oxygen uptake than untreated specimens.
At about 1000 °C in air for 50–100 hours, aluminized specimens will exhibit minimal oxide-scale growth relative to untreated specimens.
After oxidation exposure, aluminized specimens will retain the untreated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
After oxidation exposure, aluminized specimens will retain the untreated alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C.
The treatment will remain effective only if the alumina scale stays intact during exposure near 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
The treatment will not adversely affect properties under static or dynamic mechanical loading.
Changing the Hf and Ta proportions affects the strength, elastic modulus, and microstructure of Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys.
